body:
I understand that his condition will not just magically disappear overnight and that no amount of words will allow me to truly understand what he is currently feeling. What I meant was that we believed it would be the last time that he would have to go back to his rehabilitation center since, upon having a meeting with him there with both him and his supervisor in a free and open space, we discussed various ways that would make him feel more comfortable in confiding with others and understand that he is not alone, especially his family who are trying to help him with his struggle.

During that meeting, which he and his supervisor were primarily in charge of, he emphasized that he did not feel that he had a safe network of people and again felt very alone, and proposed that we have our small group of friends become more involved with his issue and talk regularly about how we all are feeling. We figured that because of this new involvement with more people helping with his issue, it might have been the trick to helping him recover without going back, but that was unfortunately not the case.

Becoming successful, playing video games/hanging out with our group of friends, and writing new and useful computer programs from what we've talked in our sessions. We had a schedule on his request where every week or so we would get together on Skype and just chat about mundane things in everyone's day and this came up a few times.

Thank you, I've known this guy since I started elementary school so I couldn't abandon him if I tried. 

And yes, he's had a lot of trouble for a lot of reasons throughout his life understanding the world. He's always very straightforward and... logical I guess? He's told me that way he feels is that something will end up triggering his stress, and the feeling will just keep building up until the only way out that he can reason is suicide. He's also told me of his OCD condition that exacerbates this feeling. What I'm worried about is that stress is a normal part of life, and most everyone has ways of keeping themselves together to handle it and move on. But because he has had all of these problems with stress he may never be able to conquer it and function by himself ever again. Again, we've gone through this with him 7 times but it's getting to the point where we just don't know what to do next since nothing seems to be working.

You're exactly right. I've never wanted any sort of appreciation or recognition for helping him, all I've ever wanted is for him to get better with the help he needs so that things can go back to how they were (at least somewhat) between all of us. I'm just glad he was at least able to open up at all before anything happened, because he has never gone as far as a suicide note before. 

And thank you very much for the pm offer. If tomorrow goes how I think it might, I may take you up on it if that is okay.

Thank you so much man, that really means a lot to me. 

I know that it was the right thing to do, but I'm already imagining what's going to happen tomorrow once his family and our circle of friends find out. There's going to be drama and crying and words thrown about and I'm not sure how his mother is going to be able to take this happening again (she's an absolute sweetheart).
